$comment: THE INSPECTOR'S PER-SCREEN PROMISE, AS DATA (RULE CFG; BATCH LE-2 V-5). sharedKeys: what a change made while another screen is being edited still writes for EVERY screen — the words, links and pictures, and the effects (the published page carries an effect for every screen: LE2-4), and what a block IS — its meaning, a heading's level, a landmark’s name, “On every page” (the page has one structure on every screen: LE8-1), and a Grid’s Column widths (drawn only where it shows all its columns, so a phone’s own would never show: LE3-6) and its As many as fit (one rule the browser applies on every screen: LE-12), and a picture's traced outline (it is the picture's, like its src: LE-13b). Everything else is that screen's own. banner / deviceTab: what the Inspector says while a screen other than the desktop is being edited; {screen} is that screen's name, {reach} the screens the change shows on (config/layout.json rungs' words, joined), {shared} the line about what stays shared.

perScreen.banner: Editing {screen} — what you change here (size, spacing, colours, fonts, backgrounds) shows on {reach}. A control that says “every screen” changes them all.
perScreen.shared: Words, links, pictures and effects are the same on every screen.
perScreen.deviceTab: You're editing {screen}. Sizes, spacing and looks you change now show on {reach}. A control marked “every screen” changes them all.
perScreen.narrowerToo: {own} — and on {narrower} too, unless you change it there

header.$comment: LE-11: the held header's controls (Placement) and the announcement bar (Meaning); pageRegions: Page settings' show / hide of the shared header and footer on one page (PS-14).
header.awayHint: It comes back when the visitor scrolls up, moves into it with the keyboard, or reaches the end of the page.
header.overHint: The first section starts at the very top, under the header. It fills in once held, so its words stay readable.
header.lastRow: Keep only the last row on screen
header.lastRowHint: The rows above it (a top bar, an announcement) scroll away; the last row stays held.

widths.$comment: BATCH LE-3: AC-9 the site's one content width (Page grid panel; a section's Content width) and AC-30 a set width (a block's Custom width on a row of the page; a Grid's Column widths). {width} is the content width in rem.
widths.contentHint: Every section of every page sits on this centred width; backgrounds still run edge to edge. A section can still be set Edge to edge.
widths.contentFullHint: Sections run the full width of the screen, inside the side space.
widths.sectionFollows: This section follows the site's content width ({width}rem, Page grid). Pick Edge to edge to let it run the full width.
widths.sectionOptsOut: This section runs the full width; the others sit on the site's content width ({width}rem).
widths.pageRowHint: A % is a share of the row. A set width (e.g. 20rem) stays that wide, and the other blocks share the rest; on a narrow screen they stack.
widths.colHint: Share columns divide what the others leave. Where the Grid shows fewer columns (a phone), they are equal again.
widths.colUneven: Column widths need every block of the Grid to be the same number of columns wide, and none placed by hand.

sizes.$comment: BATCH LE-12: SZ-4 a block's Proportion (Size), SZ-3 its Limits (Size) and a Grid column Between two widths, GR-2 a Grid's Columns As many as fit. {min} is the card width.
sizes.proportionHint: The block keeps this shape on every screen; words that need more room still make it taller. Typing a Height turns it off.
sizes.limitsHint: In rem, % or ch (e.g. 40rem, 65ch). Never wider than the screen; a max height never cuts words — they make the block taller.
sizes.fitHint: As many blocks across as fit at {min} each, on every screen; one a line on a narrow phone. Blocks keep their order.

pageRegions.header: Show the header on this page
pageRegions.footer: Show the footer on this page

pageOrder.$comment: LE8-2: Page settings — move the page one place in the order of the page tabs.

sharedRegion.$comment: PS-2 (BATCH LE-8): the Page header / Page footer's “On every page” switch under Meaning. {region} is header or footer.
sharedRegion.label: On every page
sharedRegion.on: One {region} for the whole site — what you change here changes on every page, and a page you add gets it too.
sharedRegion.off: Only on this page. Turn it on to show this {region} on every page (it takes the place of the other pages' own).

align.$comment: BATCH LE-4: AC-27 a block's Across / Down (Fill included; the nine squares set both), AC-25 Position blocks + Wrapped lines, AL-5 Text lines up, AL-6 Push to the far end. Keys are the stored values.
align.placeHint: Across and Down place just this block. Fill stretches it. Along a row or a stack a place takes the free room, so the blocks after it move with it. Auto lets it sit where the layout puts it.
align.pushHint: Moves this block — and the blocks after it — to the far end of its row or stack: a menu's last links, a card's button at the bottom. It needs room to move into: a card in a row of cards has it.
align.wrappedHint: Where the lines sit when the box is taller than they need — give it a height to see it.

flow.$comment: BATCH LE-13: FL-3 Wrap words round it (a picture in a Stack), FL-6 When it doesn't fit (a Side by side), PO-4 Overlap the section above (a page section); FL-3b (LE-13b) Words follow, shown with the wrap. Keys are the stored values; overlapSteps are the words of config/layout.json flow.overlapSteps, one each, in the same order.
flow.wrapHint: The words after this picture run beside it and then back under it. On a narrow screen the picture stops floating and the words follow it.
flow.shapeHint: Its round corners: round the picture's corners first (Rounded corners, in Outline & effects) — a circle for a head teacher's photo. A cut-out's outline: for a picture with a see-through background (a PNG); a picture from another site that does not allow it keeps to its box.
flow.fitHint: Scroll sideways keeps every block on one line that visitors swipe or scroll, a part of the next one showing. Keyboard users reach it with Tab and move it with the arrow keys.
flow.overlapHint: This section moves up over the bottom of the one above it, in front of it. The section above grows by the same amount, so nothing in it is covered.
